conviction_note: Draft sum -2.8, revised to -2.0 once the crowded short (about 22-24% of float) shrank the three guidance and capex negatives. The scaled number is -1.2: abs_move 12 (the option-implied 11.3, pushed up because a satellite-target or capex guide change is likely) times p_up 45. p_up sits only slightly below 50 because the stock is already 72% off its high and 27% down in October, and it rose ~15% today on the Rakuten JV and a Nasdaq rebound. Both measurements lean negative; the scaled one is smaller because the squeeze risk and washed-out positioning are real two-way mechanisms.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $44.4M (Zacks, cited by Earnings Whispers 2026-11-02, https://finviz.com/news/413750/ast-spacemobiles-plunge-puts-launch-cadence-and-its-150-million-revenue-floor-on-trial), $46.5M (TIKR, https://www.tikr.com/blog/ast-spacemobile-promised-150-million-heres-what-has-to-happen-next), $47.2M (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ASTS/estimates). Consensus EPS -$0.41/-$0.42 against a whisper of -$0.48. Company guide (8-K ex.99.1, 2026-08-10, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526342540/asts-ex99_1.htm): FY2026 revenue $150-200M 'on track', Q3 capex $350-425M, adjusted opex $105-115M, and about 45 satellites in orbit by early 2027. H1 revenue was $46.3M, so H2 needs $104-154M; consensus FY is about $165M with Q4 at about $72.6M. The stock trades on the deployment schedule and the forward guide more than on quarterly revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 65.87M shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, 3.2 days to cover on 20.7M ADV (massive.com quote page read 2026-11-09, https://www.massive.com/quote/asts). 65.26M shares short = 23.6% of float in a 2026-10-12 report (https://finviz.com/news/401306/ast-spacemobile-stock-rallying-after-much-needed-upgrade); Koyfin via Stocktwits gives about 19.9-21.7%. So the short is crowded at roughly 20-24% of float. Baseline: 25d skew +1.98 vol points (mild put bid, lean 'balanced'), put/call OI 0.64, ATM IV 158%, event-implied move 11.26%. Run-up -28.3% over 20d and +1.6% over 5d. The stock sits 72% below its 52-week high and 22% above its low. The intraday quote rose about 15% on 2026-11-09 (Rakuten JV and a Nasdaq rebound of about 3% from a post-election slump), so the entry close already carries a one-day squeeze-like move. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned 'bullish' about a week before the print.

findings.finding: Deployment is behind the company's own target. No BlueBird has launched since BlueBirds 11-13 on 2026-08-05, so 13 have launched and 12 work (BB7 was de-orbited). BlueBirds 14-16 reached Cape Canaveral around 2026-10-10 and still had no announced launch date on 2026-11-09. Reaching 'about 45 in orbit by early 2027' needs roughly 29-32 more satellites in 4-5 months. The 2026-11-06 8-K exhibit now frames external launch agreements as 'over 100 BlueBird satellites, to be deployed cumulatively between 2027 and 2028', so a formal cut or reframing of the early-2027 target on the call is likely. A near-term Falcon 9 date for 14-16 announced on the call would be the offsetting upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-15: the target moved from 45-60 by end-2026 to about 45 by early 2027, in the same window as the $1B convert pricing, and the stock fell 17.0% (baseline). 2026-04-23: the BB7 orbit loss cost roughly 8-18%. 2026-10-13: Piper's downgrade to a forecast of 18 satellites by end-2026 cost 5-9%. Launch successes have been bought: +6% on 2026-06-17 when BB8-10 reached orbit (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/06/17/ast-spacemobile-jumps-6-spacex-climbs-3-as-the-biggest-direct-to-phone-satellites-ever-reach-orbit/).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 26.8% in October on deployment delays, and Piper has published 18 satellites by end-2026. But the company has not withdrawn 'about 45 by early 2027'. If the market fully held a cut, the -28% 20-day run-up would not have been followed by a +15% day into the print, and the skew would not be close to flat.
findings.independence: Stocktwits 2026-10-11 (BB14-16 at the Cape, no launch date): https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/asts-stock-bluebirds-14-16-florida-fcc-sda-backed-900-mhz-test/cZx4DUVRBFg; Advanced Television 2026-10-03 (batch about a month behind, 29 more satellites needed in 4-5 months): https://www.advanced-television.com/?p=293255; Motley Fool 2026-11-03 (13 satellites today): https://www.aol.com/articles/why-shares-ast-spacemobile-slipped-160856000.html

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $150-200M has been held unchanged for three reports and is now stretched. H1 was $46.3M (Q1 $14.7M, Q2 $31.5M). Q3 consensus is about $44-47M, so the low end needs about $59M in Q4 and consensus needs about $72.6M, which is 34% above the company's best quarter ever (Q4 2025, $54.3M). Revenue is lumpy gateway hardware plus government milestones, and management has said it is weighted to Q4. A trim to the low end, a cut, or a Q3 gateway slip is a plausible guide event on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 revenue of $14.7M missed a $21M consensus and the stock moved -1.2% (baseline, 2025-11-10). The Q1 2026 miss came with a capex raise and the stock moved -11.6% (2026-05-11/12). Q2 2026 reaffirmed the guide and the stock moved +4.2%. Revenue misses alone have moved this stock little; guide and capex changes have moved it a lot.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still models about $165M for the year, inside the guide, and Q1-Q2 2027 at $100M and $131M, which depend on commercial service in 2027. If the market had priced a guide cut, consensus would sit at or below $150M and the Q4 number would not exceed the record quarter by a third.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers 2026-11-02 (the $150M floor 'on trial', Q4 needs about $59M at the low end): https://finviz.com/news/413750/ast-spacemobiles-plunge-puts-launch-cadence-and-its-150-million-revenue-floor-on-trial. Same arithmetic, different outlet; the company 8-K gives the H1 numbers.

findings.finding: The Blacklift rocket was announced 2026-11-06 (8-K item 7.01). AST pays about $800M upfront ($400M cash plus 10-14M Class A shares, about 3.3-4.7% of 299.8M outstanding), $250M for engines for the first three rockets and $250M of engineering services over three years: more than $1.3B committed. First flights are late 2028, with a new US engine plant. The Q4 capex and cash guide on the call will have to absorb it, against negative free cash flow of $719M last quarter and pro forma cash of about $3.7B at June 30, before Q3 capex of $350-425M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A capex guide raise (to $575-650M) came with the -11.6% reaction to Q1 2026. The Blacklift announcement itself was +1% to +5% in pre-market and reportedly -8% on the day 2026-11-06 (24/7 Wall St. related headline), so it was taken as a cost once digested.
findings.why_not_priced: The release gives no capex figure for the rocket or the engine plant, so the size of the cash-runway change is first quantifiable on tonight's call. If it were priced, the stock would not have gained ~15% on 2026-11-09 into the call.
findings.independence: Press coverage of the $1.3B deal and its payment structure: https://cbsaustin.com/news/local/firefly-to-supply-engines-for-ast-spacemobile-rocket-in-13b-deal; cash-burn figure: https://www.aol.com/articles/why-shares-ast-spacemobile-slipped-160856000.html

findings.finding: AST has priced large convertibles in the window around its reporting dates three times: about $1B 2036 notes on 2026-02-11, and $1.15B 2034 notes on 2026-07-15/16. Those days are in the baseline at -15.2% and -17.0%. With Blacklift's $400M cash and continued capex of $350M+ a quarter, a post-print raise inside the window is possible. Lesson 4 applied: the money buys launches, satellite production through BB51 and a $1.3B backlog, so it funds a corroborated ramp. That is why this is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Convert pricing days: 2026-02-11 -15.2%, 2026-07-15 -17.0%, 2025-10-21 -9.2% (baseline history; these are financing 8-Ks, not prints). One convert-completion day was +11% (2026-07-20, per Benzinga via Pulse2).
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing is filed: no S-3 or offering 8-K was seen in EDGAR submissions through 2026-11-06. It is a pattern, not a document, hence the small size. A market expecting it would show a steeper put skew than +2 vol points.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list (no offering filing since July): https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001780312.json

findings.finding: The definitive Rakuten AST JV was announced 2026-11-09 before the open: Rakuten holds 51% of the voting rights, an AST subsidiary 49%, up to ¥148B (about $1B) of J-LEO government support is expected, AST supplies the satellites, and service is targeted by end-March 2029. The call may quantify AST's satellite-supply revenue or capital inflow, which the release did not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The preliminary J-LEO selection was in the 2026-08-10 release (stock +4.2% next day). The definitive JV drove ~11-15% intraday on 2026-11-09, which sits before the entry close.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline is priced: the move happened today before entry. Only the AST share of the economics, still undisclosed, is unpriced.

findings.finding: Government work is building, and backlog (above $1.3B at Q2) could rise on the call. On 2026-11-05 AST disclosed a Space Force sensing award supporting prime STR (value undisclosed). The FCC granted an SDA-backed 30-day STA (2026-10-09 to 11-08) for 902-928 MHz radiolocation tests. Three awards announced earlier carry more than $100M of funded near-term value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Space Force news on 2026-11-05 was swamped by a 6% QQQ sell-off and the stock fell 15%. Government awards have not been shown to move the stock on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: The award value is undisclosed, so a backlog step-up or a quantified government revenue line on the call would be new. The market reaction on 2026-11-05 was macro, not a read of the award.

findings.finding: There is competitive and legal overhang the call will be asked about. SpaceX bought a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio from Grain that AST had pursued (2026-10-09, stock -8.5% to -10.5%). Piper cut to Neutral, PT $98 to $54, partly on SpaceX limiting launch access (2026-10-13). Viasat petitioned the FCC against AST's overseas spectrum application (around 2026-10-23, -4.3%). A securities class action is pending, with multiple law-firm solicitations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each event cost 4-10% on its day in October, so this overhang has been sold as it arrived.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced (each event was sold on the day). What remains is management's first answer on launch access, now that SpaceX is a direct competitor and the main launch provider.

findings.finding: The whisper EPS of -$0.48 is wider than the -$0.41 consensus because adjusted opex was guided to $105-115M and Q2 landed near the top of its range. An EPS miss against consensus is likely but is a reported-quarter line this name has not traded on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 EPS of -$0.66 against -$0.23 came with -11.6%, but alongside a capex raise. The Q3 2025 miss came with -1.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper is public, so this is mostly priced. It is small for that reason.

findings.finding: Positioning cuts for a bounce. 65.9M shares short (about 22-24% of float, 3.2 days to cover, 2026-10-15 settlement). findings.why_not_priced: The short base is a mechanism, not a view. If it had covered, short interest would have fallen from 65M shares; the latest settlement is about flat to the 64.8M of 2026-09-30.
